fields.v: SDD as practised with any tool; documentation of five tools read: OpenSpec v1.5.0, Spec Kit (main branch), MoAI-ADK (main branch), Conductor v0.4.1, Kiro (unversioned docs, Oct 2026). Sample covers 12 named tools (OpenSpec, Spec Kit, OpenCode, Kiro, MoAI-ADK, Codex, spec-kitty, Conductor, .specs, Trae, Claude Code, Cursor); interviewees also used Superpowers, BMAD, own tools

As prescribed by tools: Markdown spec, plan/design, task list. OpenSpec: capability specs (living) + change specs per change, archived; design in separate file. Spec Kit: numbered feature directory per change request, plan file. Kiro: requirements.md, design.md, tasks.md per feature under .kiro/specs/. Conductor: change 'tracks' with spec and plan. MoAI-ADK: spec per change, plan file. Observed content taxonomy: what (goals, requirements, acceptance, constraints, context) vs how (design, plan, code level, cross-cutting) (Table III)

Observed workflow types: (1) human-gated per change (approve each tool phase); (2) spec-gated then autonomous (approve spec, agents implement with tests, CI, reviewer agents); (3) system-level design-first. Common practice: agent drafts spec from human intent, iterative refinement, verification mainly through agent-written end-to-end/acceptance tests. Prescribed: spec -> plan/design -> tasks before implementation

Prescribed: OpenSpec none required; Spec Kit user runs each step; Kiro between phases; Conductor spec, plan, each phase; MoAI-ADK spec before implementation. Observed: most tool users read specs partially or delegated review to agents; some (mostly tool makers, organisational settings) reviewed in full; 98.3% of spec files single author, 68.5% of inline spec comments by bots
Not run by the authors; observed practice (full workflows as reported by practitioners; spec artefacts in repositories)

Not classified in Böckeler terms by the authors; observed retention practices: living spec (spec-anchored), accumulated change record, discard after implementation (spec-first); 81.5% of spec files have a single recorded commit
Mostly new features (82.0% of judged specs labelled feat); SDD skipped for small tasks, bugs, hotfixes, one-off scripts; specs also reverse-engineered in brownfield projects

21 interviews; 154 Reddit records (99 relevant) from 1,497 filtered; repository sample 266 repos / 36,890 files (13 Kiro repos, 654 requirements docs); SpecMine 470,795 spec files / 73,030 repos + 98,574 Kiro artefacts / 12,910 repos; 5,979 spec-touching PRs; 1,000 specs LLM-judged. Median 19 specs per repository, 673 words each
Open-source GitHub repositories (various); interviewees from industry (domains not stated)

21 practitioners: 8 tool makers, 13 tool users; experience <10 y (6), 10-19 (7), 20-29 (5), >=30 (3); software developer (11), founder/manager/PM (6), architect/consultant (3), researcher (1); tools: OpenSpec or derivative (7), Spec Kit or derivative (3), Superpowers (3), own tool (3), none (3), Kiro (1), BMAD (1). Solo developers and teams
None measured. Reported qualitatively: SDD runs 2-3x tokens and ~2x time vs direct prompting (one Reddit team, R41); '80% of tokens ... to make a plan' (P3); time shifts to specification
None measured (reported: more reliable agent work, not separable from model improvements; 'We couldn't prove it improved the code', R41)
None measured
None measured (cognitive load reported qualitatively: more for some users, less for some makers)

Repository measures: share of specs with implementation detail (77.6%; 58.2% a section or more); purpose labels (82.0% feat); commits per spec (81.5% single commit); authorship concentration (98.3% single author; owners + top-3 committers 90% of spec commits); bot share of inline comments (68.5%); spec count and length; section headings per template. Qualitative codes: benefits, challenges (drift, decay, evaluation effort, inertia)

Manual: inductive thematic analysis of Reddit and interview transcripts (merged codebook 427 codes; saturation tracked; no inter-rater agreement). Automatic: GitHub API mining, Markdown heading parsing, commit/PR history. LLM-as-judge (gemini-2.5-pro, temperature 0, verbatim quotes required; quotes matched 98.3%/99.4%) for content and purpose labels on 1,000 specs. Transcripts grammar-corrected by gpt-5.4-mini and checked
N/A (observational practice study; no configuration run)

No configuration comparison. Compares prescribed (tool documentation, tool makers) vs practised (tool users, repositories); concurrent triangulation of three sources; comparisons across tools on repository measures. No acceptance tests, repetitions or intervention rules (N/A)

Makers keep 'how' out of specs, users put it in (77.6% of repository specs contain implementation detail, though OpenSpec/Spec Kit tell users not to); SDD used selectively, mainly for new features; spec review partial or delegated to agents, code verified mainly through agent-written tests; retention divided (living spec / change record / discard); almost no one uses a tool as published; collaboration benefit only where specs cross roles; reliability gains reported but confounded with model improvements; cost shifts to planning (tokens, time, cognitive load); implementation drift and spec decay common; evaluation effort outgrows human review; team inertia. No statistical tests

Triangulation corroborated content and workflow findings; sources disagreed in places (Findings 3, 4), reported and interpreted. Repository evidence cannot measure benefits, effort or challenges. Limitations stated: associations not causation; single coder per source, no inter-rater agreement; self-report; volunteer and OpenSpec-heavy samples (OpenSpec 78.4% of specs); commit counts understate revision; LLM labels may be wrong; early adoption period

Difficulties of earlier spec-first practice persist (writing cost, staleness, traceability). Future work: how practitioners identify needed spec updates; whether human involvement in acceptance criteria improves verification; how SDD benefits change as models improve and teams adopt; controlled study varying implementation detail; compare spec given / spec withheld / no spec across model versions; measure drift in SpecMine. Threats: internal (associations, coder influence), construct (self-report, indirect repository measures), external (engaged volunteers, Reddit ranking, public popular repos, single-repo-dominated types, early period)
